failure-analysis.name: Failure Analysis
failure-analysis.summary: Walk through what went wrong, why, and what changes — a structured post-mortem for stakeholder reviews. Pairs honest accountability with a credible recovery plan.

beats.name: Opening Remark
beats.description: Set an empathetic, accountable tone before any analysis. Acknowledge the impact on the people in the room and the customers affected. Authenticity here earns you the credibility you'll need for the rest of the deck.

beats.name: Incident Breakdown
beats.description: Walk through what happened, in time order. Stick to facts: what systems, what users, what timeline. No causal claims yet — just an accurate, neutral reconstruction the audience can trust.

beats.name: Impact Analysis
beats.description: Quantify the damage. Customer-hours lost, revenue at risk, SLA breaches, downstream knock-ons. Be specific and direct; vague impact statements undermine the rest of the post-mortem.

beats.name: Root Cause
beats.description: Trace the failure to its underlying cause, not the most visible symptom. Use a 'five whys' or fishbone framing if useful. Distinguish between the proximate trigger and the systemic conditions that allowed it.

beats.name: Proposed Solutions
beats.description: Present the corrective actions you're taking. Lead with the highest-leverage fix; sequence the rest. For each action, name an owner and a date — solutions without owners are aspirations.

beats.name: Action Plan
beats.description: Lay out the rollout: what ships when, how it's verified, who signs off. Show that 'fixed' has a definition and a deadline, not just intent.

beats.name: Evaluate Outcome
beats.description: Define the metrics that will tell you the fix worked. Pre/post comparisons, monitoring SLOs, error budgets — whatever proves the failure mode is closed and not just deferred.

beats.name: Lessons Learned
beats.description: Distill the broader lessons that outlive this specific incident. What does the team or organization now know that it didn't before? What patterns will you watch for elsewhere?

beats.name: Preventive Measures
beats.description: List the systemic safeguards being added — process changes, automated checks, on-call procedures, review gates. Show how this category of failure becomes harder to recur, not just this specific instance.

beats.name: Closing Thoughts
beats.description: Close with humility and forward momentum. Re-affirm accountability, thank the audience for their patience, and signal confidence in the path forward without overclaiming.

regulatory.name: Regulatory / Compliance
regulatory.summary: Government agencies, auditors, or compliance bodies reviewing adherence to rules and standards.
regulatory.description: Government agencies, auditors, and compliance bodies reviewing adherence to rules and standards. Lead with evidence, date-stamp material, cite document references, and map each claim to the requirement it satisfies. Moderate chart density; 20-40 slides with an appendix.

all-hands.name: All Hands
all-hands.summary: The full company — mixed roles, mixed seniority, looking for context, signal, and inclusion.
all-hands.description: An all-hands audience spans the whole company. Frame the period in terms anyone can grasp: what we did, what mattered, and what's next. Highlight people and teams; surface successes and challenges; close on a forward-looking note. Avoid lapsing into function-specific jargon.

persuade.name: Persuade
persuade.summary: Change belief or win support for a specific argument, idea, or recommendation.
persuade.description: Use when the audience may be skeptical or undecided. Build a crisp thesis, support it with evidence, address objections, and end with a clear action.
persuade.outcome: The audience accepts the argument or supports the recommendation.

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Precise, evidence-led voice for engineering, research, and product-detail audiences.
technical.description: Lead with the question or claim, then walk through the mechanism and the numbers. Use exact terminology; assume the audience can handle and prefers it. Diagrams, tables, and benchmarks are first-class.
voiceCues: State the claim, then the mechanism, then the evidence.
Use exact terminology — don't soften technical terms for general readability.
Quote benchmarks with conditions (cold/warm, p50/p95/p99, dataset, hardware).
Prefer diagrams and tables over prose paragraphs for structural information.
samplePhrases: p95 inference latency is 38ms on a single A100, down from 312ms on the prior runtime.
We replaced the streaming serializer with a batched protobuf path; throughput rose 4.2× under load.
The result holds for context windows up to 32k tokens; beyond that, see appendix B.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
